author: Han Li
description:
China’s economic growth is expected to slow further next year as export strength fades and weak domestic demand persists, even as the global economy remains resilient, according to a new outlook from the Peterson Institute for International Economics (PIIE).
The Washington-based think tank projects China’s GDP will grow 4.6 per cent this year and 4.3 per cent in 2027, down from 5 per cent growth in 2025, according to its semi-annual Global Economic Prospects report, released on Tuesday.
The...
title: China’s economy to slow as global growth stays solid, US think tank report says

author: Teresa Elena Frontado,Lucy Quaggin
description:
Los Angeles County prosecutors are seeking bail of US$100 million each for a Chinese-born couple charged on Tuesday with conspiring to abuse young children who were born through surrogacy and raised in their California mansion.
Guojun Xuan, 66, and Silvia Zhang, 39, allegedly directed nannies to physically punish the children, watched the beatings through an extensive surveillance system and coached children before police arrived to deny the abuse, according to a felony complaint.
At least 14...
title: US seeks US$100 million bail each for Chinese-born couple in surrogacy child abuse case

author: Victoria Bela
description:
Chinese researchers have developed a “lifelike” shape-changing hydrogel they say could provide a platform for next-generation developments, such as flexible tissue engineering scaffolds, brain-computer interfaces and humanlike robots.
Inspired by living organisms, the team created a light-triggered system called STERS, which uses liquid metal particles to generate slow, self-sustaining chemical reactions that allow a hydrogel to change its structure over time.
Capable of growing and changing...
title: Chinese team creates ‘lifelike’ hydrogel that changes shape for smart devices

author: Lawrence Chung
description:
Two combat-tested American drones could become part of Taiwan’s expanding unmanned arsenal as the island seeks to build a “drone shield” against the People’s Liberation Army.
California-based defence technology company Aevex Aerospace is working with Taiwan’s Coretronic Intelligent Robotics Corporation (CIRC) to produce its Vandal and Onyx drones locally, combining lessons drawn from the war in Ukraine with the island’s electronics and manufacturing capabilities.
Both aircraft have been tested...
title: US firm to make battle-tested drones in Taiwan, boosting supply chain resilience

author: Fan Chen
description:
China has pledged to expand its health partnership with Kazakhstan by helping the Central Asian nation integrate traditional medicine directly into its national healthcare system, shifting away from simple product exports.
The Chinese embassy in Kazakhstan on Monday called for the alignment of high-level policy to enhance bilateral health cooperation for both countries’ benefit.
“Both nations should promote the qualitative upgrading of cooperation in smart healthcare, hi-tech diagnostics and...
title: How traditional Chinese medicine is shaping Kazakhstan’s health system

author: Liu Zhen
description:
Indonesia is expected to receive its first Chengdu J-10CE fighter jets in six months, according to an Indonesian media report, which would make it the third international operator of the Chinese-made aircraft.
Jakarta confirmed an order of 42 of the 4.5-generation fighter jets – known as Vigorous Dragons – last October, with an approved budget of US$9 billion.
The first delivery is expected in April though it is not known how many aircraft will be delivered, Indonesian news outlet Republika...
title: Indonesia to take delivery of first Chinese J-10CE fighter jets in 6 months, report says

author: Brian Rhoads,Raymond Ma
description:
Germany and France, the European Union’s two largest economies, jointly called for tougher EU trade defences, as European and Chinese negotiators prepare for crunch talks this week under the shadow of a potential trade war.
“The open and rules-based trade system is massively affected by weaponisation of trade, systemic market-distorting practices, and global macroeconomic imbalances,” German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and French President Emmanuel Macron said in an open letter. “We need urgent...
title: Germany joins France in call for China trade defences

author: Zhou Xiaoming
description:
The recent US-China summit yielded a narrow, caution-filled outcome for bilateral trade: a two-month extension of the Kuala Lumpur trade truce, which now expires on January 10 next year. This reprieve eases fears of immediate tariff escalation and shows that head-of-state diplomacy can still curb spiralling confrontation. Yet the short timeline exposes the wide gulf separating the two sides’ priorities.
China’s position has been unambiguous: removal of all punitive tariffs and restrictive...
title: Short trade truce can’t paper over realities of US-China relationship

author: Eve Qiao
description:
China tried three times to persuade powerful families in northern Myanmar to shut down scam operations before Myanmar police made a massive arrest in 2023, according to a new documentary broadcast on Chinese state television.
The three-part documentary, which was jointly produced by China’s Ministry of Public Security and state broadcaster CCTV and began airing on Monday, shows obstacles faced by Chinese authorities in pursuing criminal networks and scam groups operating in northern Myanmar...
title: China tried 3 times to talk crime families out of scam business in Myanmar: state media

author: Gabriel Dominguez
description:
Turkmenistan has added the FK-2000 missile-and-gun system to its growing arsenal of Chinese-made air defences, highlighting Beijing’s expanding role in the Central Asian weapons market once dominated by Russia.
At least 10 FK-2000 vehicles – along with an array of other Chinese-made military equipment – could be seen in footage of Turkmenistan’s Independence Day parade in Ashgabat on September 27.
Developed by the state-owned China Aerospace Science and Industry Corporation, the FK-2000 is a...
title: Turkmenistan grows its arsenal of Chinese air defences as Russia’s role shrinks

author: Amber Wang
description:
In 2019, President Xi Jinping became the first Chinese leader to publicly call for the exploration of detailed proposals for governing Taiwan after reunification.
Seven years later, the first proposals from a handful of the mainland’s leading research institutes have either been finalised or are nearing completion, the South China Morning Post has learned.
Rather than setting out a single fixed model, scholars involved in those studies told the SCMP there should be different scenarios based on...
title: Beijing’s policy advisers map out how post-reunification Taiwan could be governed

author: Chow Chung-yan
description:
Beijing’s push to accumulate gold serves a larger goal: yuan internationalisation. In this series, Part I traces China’s path to becoming a gold superpower, while this article explores Hong Kong’s key role in safeguarding the nation’s financial security.
In 2013, one-third of the world’s traded gold passed through Hong Kong. That year, the city imported 1,158 tonnes of bullion, overtaking India, the traditional top buyer. For all our love of the glittering metal, little of it stayed in our...
title: Hong Kong’s bridge of gold completes China’s yuan ambition
